en: close aide; confidant (of a powerful person)

examples.en: The president's close aide quit the company.
He worked for a long time as the chairman's right-hand man.
Only the inner circle knows that secret.

examples.ko: 가수의 측근에 따르면 다음 달에 앨범이 나와요.
examples.en: According to people close to the singer, an album comes out next month.

examples.ko: 감독은 믿을 수 있는 측근에게 일을 맡겼어요.
examples.en: The director entrusted the work to a close aide he could trust.
The president talked separately with a close aide.

explain: 힘 있는 사람 곁에서 일하는 가까운 사람에게 써요. '대통령 측근', '회장 측근'처럼 뉴스에서 자주 나와요. 친한 친구에게는 쓰지 않고 '친한 사람'이나 '믿는 사람'이라고 말해요.

phrases.en: He is the chairman's closest aide.
phrases.nuance_ko: 측근 중에서도 가장 가까운 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the very closest person among one's aides.

phrases.en: The president's aides gathered for a meeting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가까운 사람이 여러 명일 때 복수로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The plural form for when there are several close aides.

phrases.example: 측근에 따르면 그는 곧 은퇴할 거예요.
phrases.en: According to people close to him, he will retire soon.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 소식을 전할 때 자주 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase used to report news in the media.

explain_en: Used for people who work close to someone powerful. It appears in the news in phrases like '대통령 측근' and '회장 측근'. For a close friend you wouldn't use it; you would say '친한 사람' or '믿는 사람' instead.

examples.ko: 그 나라의 통치자는 오랫동안 바뀌지 않았어요.
examples.en: The ruler of that country did not change for a long time.
I read stories about ancient rulers in a history book.

examples.ko: 좋은 통치자는 국민의 이야기를 잘 들어요.
examples.en: A good ruler listens well to the people.
When the ruler changed, the mood of the country changed too.
That king is remembered as a wise ruler.
The ruler in the drama was a frightening person.

explain: '통치자'는 나라나 지역을 다스리는 사람을 넓게 가리켜요. '왕', '황제', '대통령'처럼 정해진 직함이 아니라 역할을 말할 때 편해요. 역사 이야기나 뉴스에서 자주 써요.

phrases.example: 그 나라의 최고 통치자가 국민 앞에서 연설했어요.
phrases.en: The country's supreme ruler gave a speech in front of the people.
phrases.nuance_ko: '통치자'보다 가장 높은 자리에 있는 사람을 분명히 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you want to clearly point to the person at the very top, more specific than plain '통치자'.

phrases.en: He became a ruler at a young age.
phrases.nuance_ko: '통치자'를 주어나 보어로 써서 어떤 자리에 오르는 것을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses '통치자' as a role someone takes on, to talk about rising to power.

phrases.en: The country's leader greeted the people.
phrases.nuance_ko: '통치자'보다 부드럽고 일상적인 말이에요. 다스리는 힘보다 앞에서 이끄는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Softer and more everyday than '통치자'; it stresses leading rather than governing power.

explain_en: '통치자' broadly refers to whoever governs a country or region. It is handy when you mean the role rather than a fixed title like '왕', '황제', or '대통령'. You see it often in history and news.

examples.en: He complained that his mother favors only his younger brother.

examples.ko: 선생님이 특정 학생을 편애하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: A teacher must not play favorites with certain students.

examples.ko: 편애하는 부모 밑에서 자란 사람은 마음이 불안할 때가 있어요.
examples.en: People who grew up with parents who played favorites are sometimes insecure.

examples.ko: 저는 누구도 편애하지 않고 똑같이 대해요.
examples.en: I don't favor anyone and treat everybody the same.
My grandmother especially favored her grandson.

examples.ko: 사장이 자기 사람만 편애해서 직원들이 화가 났어요.
examples.en: The boss favors only his own people, so the employees got angry.

explain: '동생을 편애하다'처럼 '을/를'과 함께 써요. 보통 불공평하다는 불만이 담긴 말이라 부모, 선생님, 상사가 한쪽만 아낄 때 많이 나와요.

phrases.en: A teacher who plays favorites loses trust.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-는'으로 뒤의 사람을 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe the person that follows.

phrases.en: My parents did not play favorites among siblings.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공평하게 대했다는 말을 부정형으로 표현해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Expresses fair treatment in the negative.

phrases.example: 팀장님이 한 사람만 편애하는 것 같아요.
phrases.en: It seems the team leader favors only one person.
phrases.nuance_ko: 확실하지 않지만 그렇게 느낀다고 조심스럽게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say carefully that it feels that way.

explain_en: It takes an object, as in '동생을 편애하다'. It usually carries a complaint about unfairness, so it often comes up when a parent, teacher or boss favors one side.

en: to threaten; to intimidate; to blackmail

examples.en: A stranger threatened me over the phone.
He blackmails his friend, saying he'll spread the secret.
Threatening people is a crime.

examples.ko: 누가 협박해도 돈을 주면 안 돼요.
examples.en: Even if someone threatens you, you must not give money.

examples.ko: 영화에서 악당이 주인공을 협박하는 장면이 나와요.
examples.en: In the movie, there's a scene where the villain threatens the hero.

examples.ko: 협박하고 도망간 범인을 경찰이 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: The police are looking for the criminal who threatened someone and ran away.

explain: '위협하다'는 무서운 상황이나 힘으로 위험을 주는 것이고, '협박하다'는 나쁜 일을 하겠다고 말해서 상대가 원하지 않는 것을 하게 만드는 거예요. 사람이 사람에게 하는 행동이라 주로 범죄나 뉴스에서 봐요. 장난으로 하는 말은 보통 '겁주다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: He was threatened by a stranger.
phrases.nuance_ko: 피해자 입장에서 말할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing used from the victim's point of view.

phrases.en: I got a threatening call yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 전화로 위협하는 경우를 가리키는 명사 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A noun phrase for threats made by phone.

phrases.en: Please don't threaten me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그만하라고 단호하게 말할 때 쓰는 존댓말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A firm polite request to stop.

explain_en: 위협하다 means to endanger by force or a frightening situation, while 협박하다 means making someone do what they don't want by promising something bad. It is a person-to-person act and appears mostly in crime news. For a joking scare, people usually say 겁주다.

examples.en: The court cut the defendant's sentence in half.
They say it was decided to reduce the sentence because it was a first offense and he is sorry.

examples.ko: 판사가 형량을 감형해 줄지는 아직 몰라요.
examples.en: We don't know yet whether the judge will reduce the sentence.

examples.ko: 대통령이 일부 수감자의 형을 감형한다고 발표했어요.
examples.en: The president announced that the sentences of some prisoners would be reduced.

examples.ko: 합의가 이루어지면 법원이 감형할 가능성이 있어요.
examples.en: If a settlement is reached, the court may reduce the sentence.
The family cried because the court did not reduce the sentence.

explain: 주어는 보통 법원, 판사, 대통령처럼 형을 정하는 쪽이에요. 형을 받는 사람의 입장에서는 '감형을 받다'라고 말해요. 일상에서는 '형을 줄여 주다'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: The judge reduced the sentence.
phrases.nuance_ko: '감형하다'를 일상적인 말로 풀어 쓴 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A plain everyday way to say 감형하다.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 반성문을 내고 감형을 받았어요.
phrases.en: He submitted a letter of remorse and got his sentence reduced.
phrases.nuance_ko: 형을 받는 사람의 입장에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the point of view of the person whose sentence is cut.

phrases.en: The 5-year prison term was reduced to 3 years.
phrases.nuance_ko: 법원 같은 쪽의 결정으로 형이 줄어든 결과를 말하는 피동 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The passive form, focusing on the result that a sentence was reduced by a court's decision.

explain_en: The subject is usually the side that decides the sentence, such as a court, judge or the president. From the point of view of the person sentenced, you say '감형을 받다'. In everyday speech people also say '형을 줄여 주다'.

examples.en: My parents are fiercely opposed to my marriage.
The residents fiercely opposed building a waste facility.
I am dead set against that plan.

examples.ko: 결사반대 구호를 외치며 시청 앞에 모였어요.
examples.en: They gathered in front of City Hall shouting slogans of fierce opposition.
The union announced it would fiercely oppose the restructuring.
Everyone shouted their strong opposition, but only I agreed.

explain: 목숨을 걸 듯 아주 강하게 반대한다는 느낌이에요. 보통 '결사반대하다'나 '결사반대를 외치다'로 쓰고, 시위 구호에서 많이 들려요. 가볍게 '엄마가 결사반대야'처럼 과장해서 말하기도 해요.

phrases.en: Citizens shouted their fierce opposition in the square.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시위나 집회에서 큰 소리로 반대 뜻을 밝힐 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when loudly voicing opposition at a protest or rally.

phrases.en: I am strongly against that plan.
phrases.nuance_ko: '이다'를 붙여 자기 입장을 강하게 말하는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '이다', a strong way to state your own position.

phrases.example: 주민들이 공사를 막으려고 결사반대 시위를 했어요.
phrases.en: Residents held a protest of fierce opposition to stop the construction.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에 붙여서 강한 반대 행동을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Placed before a noun to describe a strongly opposing action.

explain_en: It carries the feeling of opposing something as if staking your life on it. It is usually used as '결사반대하다' or '결사반대를 외치다', and is common in protest slogans. People also use it playfully, like '엄마가 결사반대야'.

examples.ko: 두 팀이 우승을 두고 치열한 경합을 벌였어요.
examples.en: The two teams had a fierce contest for the championship.

examples.ko: 여당과 야당이 경합하는 지역이라서 관심이 커요.
examples.en: The ruling and opposition parties are competing in this area, so there is a lot of interest.

examples.ko: 오랜 경합 끝에 우리 회사가 계약을 따냈어요.
examples.en: After a long contest, our company won the contract.

examples.ko: 경합 지역에서는 표 차이가 아주 작아요.
examples.en: In swing districts, the vote gap is very small.
Several companies jumped into the bidding contest.
Competition was so intense that prices dropped a lot.

explain: '경쟁'보다 실력이 비슷한 상대끼리 팽팽하게 맞서는 느낌이 있어요. 선거, 스포츠, 입찰 뉴스에서 '경합을 벌이다', '경합 지역'처럼 자주 써요.

phrases.example: 두 회사가 새 시장에서 경합하고 있어요.
phrases.en: The two companies are competing in the new market.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '경합'을 동사로 바꾼 말이고, 비슷한 힘을 가진 둘이 맞설 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form of 경합, used when two evenly matched sides face off.

phrases.example: 이번 선거에서는 경합 지역이 가장 중요해요.
phrases.en: In this election, the battleground districts matter most.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어느 쪽이 이길지 모르는 지역을 가리키는 뉴스 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A news expression for districts where the winner is hard to predict.

phrases.en: The competition between the two players is really fierce.
phrases.nuance_ko: '경합'보다 더 넓은 말이라서 실력이 달라도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: A broader word than 경합; it can be used even when the sides differ in ability.

explain_en: Compared with '경쟁', it suggests evenly matched rivals going head to head. You will see it in election, sports and bidding news in phrases like '경합을 벌이다' and '경합 지역' (swing district).

examples.en: It is not easy to give up your vested interests.
He is a young politician who challenges the establishment.
When the establishment came up, the debate heated up.

examples.ko: 기득권이 있는 사람들이 법 개정에 반대했어요.
examples.en: People with vested interests opposed the revision of the law.

examples.ko: 기득권 싸움 때문에 일이 자꾸 늦어져요.
examples.en: Because of the fight over vested interests, things keep getting delayed.
I want to give up my vested position and start anew.

explain: 이미 가지고 있는 권리나 이익을 말하는데, 뉴스에서는 '기득권을 지키다/내려놓다'처럼 변화를 막는 쪽의 이야기로 많이 나와요. 이미 힘이 있는 집단은 '기득권층'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: The establishment often dislikes change.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 힘이 있는 집단을 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the group that already holds power.

phrases.en: They are trying to protect their vested interests.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가진 것을 잃지 않으려 한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means trying not to lose what one already has.

phrases.en: They are people who have enjoyed privileges for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 가진 이익을 계속 쓰고 있다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Suggests continuing to enjoy benefits already held.

explain_en: It refers to rights or benefits someone already holds, and in the news it often comes up on the side resisting change, as in '기득권을 지키다/내려놓다'. A group that already holds power is called '기득권층'.

examples.ko: 그 후보는 아쉽게도 몇 표 차이로 낙선했어요.
examples.en: Unfortunately, that candidate lost the election by a few votes.
He said that if he loses this time, he will quit politics.

examples.ko: 시장 선거에서 낙선한 사람이 지금은 교수로 일해요.
examples.en: The person who lost the mayoral election now works as a professor.

examples.ko: 아무리 열심히 해도 낙선할 수 있다는 걸 알고 있어요.
examples.en: I know that no matter how hard I try, I could lose the election.

examples.ko: 우리 동네 의원은 지난번에 낙선해서 다시 출마했어요.
examples.en: Our neighborhood lawmaker lost last time and ran again.

examples.ko: 낙선하지 않으려고 후보들이 거리에서 인사를 해요.
examples.en: The candidates greet people on the street so they won't lose the election.

explain: 선거에서 떨어진다는 뜻이고, 반대말은 '당선되다'예요. 주어는 후보 같은 사람이에요. 시험에 떨어질 때는 '떨어지다'를 써요.

phrases.en: According to the polls, he looks likely to lose.
phrases.nuance_ko: 결과가 나오기 전에 추측할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to guess before the result is announced.

phrases.en: The candidate who lost accepted the result.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거형으로 꾸며 선거에서 진 사람을 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the past form to refer to someone who lost an election.

phrases.en: He lost in the last election.
phrases.nuance_ko: '선거에서'를 붙이면 어떤 일에서 떨어졌는지 분명해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '선거에서' makes clear what he lost.

explain_en: It means to fail to win an election, and its opposite is '당선되다'. The subject is a person such as a candidate. For failing an exam, use '떨어지다' instead.

en: troubles both at home and abroad

examples.en: The company is suffering from troubles both inside and out.
That country collapsed amid trouble at home and abroad.
Troubles at home and abroad piled up, and the government faced a crisis.

examples.ko: 뉴스에서 우리 경제가 내우외환 상황이라고 말했어요.
examples.en: The news said our economy is in a situation of trouble on all sides.

examples.ko: 내우외환을 이겨 내려면 모두 힘을 모아야 해요.
examples.en: To overcome troubles at home and abroad, everyone has to join forces.

examples.ko: 지금 팀은 내부 갈등에 성적 부진까지, 그야말로 내우외환이에요.
examples.en: The team now has internal conflict and poor results too; it truly is trouble on every side.

explain: 안의 걱정과 밖의 걱정이 함께 있다는 한자말이에요. 나라, 회사, 팀처럼 큰 단위가 안팎으로 어려울 때 쓰고, 뉴스나 글에서 자주 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 '안팎으로 힘들다'처럼 풀어서 말하기도 해요.

phrases.example: 그 회사는 몇 해째 내우외환을 겪고 있어요.
phrases.en: That company has been going through troubles both at home and abroad for several years.
phrases.nuance_ko: 큰 조직이 안팎으로 어려운 상황에 놓였을 때 쓰는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation for a large organization in trouble on all fronts.
phrases.en_equiv: to go through troubles at home and abroad

phrases.en: The country fell into trouble both at home and abroad, so people were anxious.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어려움에서 헤어나기 힘든 상태를 강조할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Emphasizes being stuck in a hard situation that is difficult to escape.
phrases.en_equiv: to be caught in troubles from within and without

phrases.en: These days our team is struggling both inside and outside.
phrases.nuance_ko: '내우외환'을 일상 대화에서 풀어서 말하는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A plain, conversational way to express 'troubles at home and abroad'.
phrases.en_equiv: to have a hard time on all sides

explain_en: It is a Sino-Korean word for having worries both inside and outside. It is used when a large unit like a country, company or team faces trouble on all sides, and it appears often in news and writing. In everyday talk people may say it plainly, like '안팎으로 힘들다'.

examples.en: The workers held a sit-in in front of the factory.
Students are staging a sit-in at the president's office.
The sit-in has been going on for ten days.
The residents began a sit-in in opposition to the construction.
The sit-in didn't stop even in cold weather.
Citizens sent food to the sit-in tent.

explain: 농성은 자기 주장을 알리려고 한곳에 자리를 잡고 계속 머무르는 시위예요. '농성을 하다', '농성에 들어가다', '농성 중이다'처럼 써요. 길을 걸으며 하는 '행진'이나 구호를 외치는 '시위'와 달리 같은 장소에서 오래 머문다는 점이 특징이에요.

phrases.en: The employees staged a sit-in in front of the company.
phrases.nuance_ko: 농성을 시작해서 계속 이어 간다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means starting a sit-in and carrying it on.

phrases.en: The union began a sit-in yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 농성을 새로 시작할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a sit-in newly begins.

phrases.en: Many people gathered at the sit-in site.
phrases.nuance_ko: 농성을 하는 장소를 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the place where a sit-in is held.

explain_en: Nongseong is a protest where people settle in one place and stay to make their point. Typical forms are 농성을 하다, 농성에 들어가다, and 농성 중이다. Unlike a march (행진) or a rally with slogans (시위), the key feature is staying in the same place for a long time.

examples.ko: 작은 잘못을 묵인하면 같은 일이 또 생겨요.
examples.en: If you let small mistakes slide, the same thing will happen again.

examples.ko: 회사가 불법 행위를 묵인했다는 기사가 나왔어요.
examples.en: An article came out saying the company tolerated illegal activity.

examples.ko: 선생님의 묵인 덕분에 교실에서 몰래 간식을 먹었어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the teacher looking the other way, I secretly ate a snack in class.

examples.ko: 이번 한 번만 모르는 척 묵인해 주실 수 있어요?
examples.en: Could you just pretend not to notice this one time?

examples.ko: 규칙 위반을 묵인하는 분위기가 가장 큰 문제예요.
examples.en: An atmosphere that tolerates rule violations is the biggest problem.

examples.ko: 부모님의 묵인이 있어서 늦게까지 놀 수 있었어요.
examples.en: My parents turned a blind eye, so I was able to stay out late.

explain: 보통 '묵인하다', '묵인해 주다' 꼴로 써요. 말로 허락하는 '허락'과 달리 알면서도 모른 척 두는 느낌이라 주로 좋지 않은 일에 나와요. 일상에서는 '눈감아 주다'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: The teacher did not let the lie slide.
phrases.nuance_ko: 알면서도 모른 척 그냥 두는 동사 꼴이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form: knowing about something but pretending not to.

phrases.en: The boss let this lateness slide.
phrases.nuance_ko: 누군가의 잘못을 봐준다는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Carries a sense of letting someone's fault go.

phrases.en: Please just overlook it this once.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '묵인'과 같은 뜻으로 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy everyday expression with the same meaning.

explain_en: It is usually used as '묵인하다' or '묵인해 주다'. Unlike '허락' (clear permission), it feels like knowing about something and pretending not to, so it mostly goes with bad things. In daily talk people also say '눈감아 주다'.

examples.ko: 경찰은 물리력을 쓰지 않고 시위대를 설득했어요.
examples.en: The police persuaded the protesters without using physical force.

examples.ko: 그 나라는 물리력보다 대화로 문제를 풀고 싶어 해요.
examples.en: That country wants to solve the problem by talking rather than by force.
An attitude of trying to settle things by force is not good.

examples.ko: 그는 물리력이 아니라 말로 사람들을 움직였어요.
examples.en: He moved people with words, not with force.
The use of physical force is strictly limited by law.
They proposed negotiating without relying on force.

explain: 뉴스나 정치, 법 이야기에서 힘으로 막거나 누르는 것을 가리킬 때 써요. 일상에서는 그냥 '힘'이나 '완력'이라고 해요. '물리력 행사', '물리력을 동원하다'처럼 한자어 동사와 함께 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 경찰이 물리력을 행사할 때는 규칙이 있어요.
phrases.en: There are rules for when the police use physical force.
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘을 실제로 쓴다는 뜻의 딱딱한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A formal phrase for actually using force.

phrases.en: The government said it would not mobilize physical force.
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘을 모아서 쓰려고 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when force is being gathered and brought in.

phrases.example: 사람들을 물리력으로 막는 것은 좋은 방법이 아니에요.
phrases.en: Stopping people by force is not a good way.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대화 대신 힘으로 하는 방법을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes using force instead of talking.

explain_en: It is used in news, politics and law to refer to stopping or pressing someone with force. In daily life people just say '힘' or '완력'. It often appears in set phrases like '물리력 행사' (use of force) and '물리력을 동원하다' (mobilize force).

examples.en: In court, the lawyer defended his client.

examples.ko: 친구가 잘못했을 때도 저는 늘 친구를 변호해요.
examples.en: Even when my friend is in the wrong, I always stand up for them.
Nobody spoke up for him.

examples.ko: 억울한 사람을 변호하고 싶어서 법대에 갔어요.
examples.en: I went to law school because I wanted to defend wronged people.

examples.ko: 동생을 변호하는 엄마의 말에 형이 화가 났어요.
examples.en: The older brother got angry at his mother's words defending the younger one.
Who will speak up for me?

explain: 법정에서 변호사가 하는 일에도 쓰고, 일상에서 누군가의 편을 들어 말해 줄 때도 써요. 일상에서는 '편들다', '감싸 주다'가 더 가벼운 말이에요. '~을/를 변호하다' 형태로 써요.

phrases.example: 그 변호사가 제 사건의 변호를 맡았어요.
phrases.en: That lawyer took charge of defending my case.
phrases.nuance_ko: 법정에서 변호하는 일을 맡을 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing used when taking on a legal defense.

phrases.example: 동생이 싸우면 저는 항상 동생 편을 들어요.
phrases.en: When my sibling fights, I always take their side.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 누군가를 변호할 때 가볍게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A light everyday way to say you stand up for someone.

phrases.en: When my friend makes a mistake, I cover for them.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잘못한 사람을 따뜻하게 보호해 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when kindly protecting someone who made a mistake.

explain_en: It describes a lawyer's work in court, and also speaking up on someone's side in daily life. In everyday talk '편들다' and '감싸 주다' are lighter. It takes the pattern '~을/를 변호하다'.

dis.h: act as defender; speak up for someone
gh: stand up for a person or idea
argue a case in court or debate

p.n: 변호 is defending the person; 변론 is arguing the case.
